collectorNotes: The vendor's launch blog (its table is embedded in the page JS) lists more benchmarks than the HF card image. Beyond the image's six, it adds Toolathlon Verified 78.4, OSWorld 2.0 59.1 and NL2Repo 56.3; NL2Repo is outside the 16 columns. The vendor's Terminal Bench 2.1 score (84.3) is a different benchmark and is not recorded. ALE 26.3 matches the official board's pass rate for the comparison models (Opus 4.8 at 27.0, GLM-5.2 at 20.4), so it is marked non-comparable, and agents-last-exam goes in not_found. OSWorld 2.0 59.1 is not labeled partial or binary. It is inferred to be partial because the same table's Opus 4.8 value of 54.8 equals the official partialScore. The model is absent from the Zapier AutomationBench, ALE, OSWorld 2, tbench Science and Scale HLE boards. Vals' Terminal-Bench 4.0 board does not list the Flash variant either; only GLM 5.3 is there. Artificial Analysis numbers were deliberately left out, except the vendor-printed GDPval-AA v2 Elo of 1773. No other vendor's comparison table showing this model was found in the leads.
verifierSummary: I opened all 12 records' sources (Z.ai blog JS bundle, deepswe.datacurve.ai, tbench.ai 4.0, frontierswe.com, toolathlon.xyz, vals.ai, plus the agents-last-exam.org API, the official OSWorld 2.0 page and the Zapier board for cross-checks). All 12 numbers appear verbatim for GLM-5.3-Flash, and the comparability flags follow the column rules. Points to tighten: (1) The blog's DeepSWE footnote only says mini-swe-agent, temperature=0.95, top_p=1.0, 6h, 400K; it never says max effort, so "默认 max effort" in #0 is an inference. (2) The OSWorld 2.0 metric in #4 can be confirmed as Partial Score: the Opus 4.8 comparison value in the same table is 54.8, and the official osworld-v2.xlang.ai page says "Claude Opus 4.8 ... completes only 20.6% of tasks at a 54.8% partial score". (3) The ALE value in #8 can be confirmed as Pass rate: in the ALE API the full-split pass rates are glm-5-2 claude_code max 0.2039, claude-opus-4-8 thinking-max 0.2697 and GPT-5.6-Terra reasoning-max 0.2796, which match the blog's 20.4/27/28. The API has no GLM-5.3-Flash row. (4) The Zapier official board has no GLM-5.3-Flash. Zapier states that leaderboard scores come from a private held-out set and that the 600 public tasks are for research only. The vendor's v1.0.6 run, with the PR #13 fix applied, was most likely on the public set, so matchesPreferred=false in #7 is appropriate. (5) In #2, tbench.ai labels reasoning_effort as none, and it is the only GLM-5.3-Flash entry.
